children: Airbus (EADSY), the global aircraft and defense manufacturer, rose approximately 0.7% to $57.82 Friday after reaching a preliminary deal with four Spanish unions. The proposal targets pay and working conditions after weeks of strikes. But the fight is not finished. Workers must still approve the agreement in a binding referendum.

Airbus needs every production line humming. Its half-year results showed 351 commercial-aircraft deliveries, 33.2 billion of revenue and 2.7 billion of adjusted EBIT. The backlog stands at a massive 9,222 jets, while management is targeting approximately 870 deliveries this year.

That backlog equals roughly 10.6 years of production at the current annual target. Airbus's approximately 15,000 Spanish employees represent nearly 8.9% of its global workforce, so another breakdown would hit far beyond Spain. The stock now trades 10.32% above its $52.41 GF Value, suggesting investors are already pricing in cleaner execution. Labor peace would protect the delivery ramp. A no vote would put the bottleneck risk straight back on the runway.

title: Airbus Rises as Its 9,222-Jet Backlog Gets Labor Relief
